transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. I came in today because... well, I keep hearing Garrett's voice. It's as clear as if he's standing right behind me, like when I'm out on the trail or just sitting in my painting room. 

I mean, logically, part of me knows he's dead. But in the moment it happens, it feels completely real to me. So, I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.
When you hear Garrett's voice, do you believe he's actually there speaking to you, or do you know it's something your mind is creating?

Well, like I was just saying, it really depends on the exact moment. Right when I hear him, I completely believe he's there. The voice is so clear that I'll actually turn around expecting to see him standing right behind me. 

It's only after a minute or two that the rational part of my brain catches up. That's when I remember that he's gone, so it has to be my mind making it up. But in that split second when it happens? No, I don't think it's my imagination at all. It feels entirely real to me.
When did you first start hearing Garrett's voice? Was it something that began suddenly over days, or has this been building up over weeks or months?

It started pretty suddenly, actually. I only started hearing his voice during this... this stretch of time recently where I was just completely wired. I was barely sleeping at all, maybe an hour or two a night, and I was taking on all these impossible projects. I just felt this intense drive to keep going and going. 

I had never heard him like that before this shift happened. I mean, I've grieved him, of course, but this wasn't like ordinary grief. It only started when my mood got really sped up like that.

Before this recent stretch where you were barely sleeping and heard Garrett's voice, have you ever had other periods in your life where you felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep, and felt like you could do anything—times that were noticeably different from your normal self?

Well, yes, actually. I mean, during this recent time, at first I felt... almost lit up, I guess you could say. Like I had this urgent purpose that no one else could see or understand. I felt like I could take on the world. 

But then... well, if anyone questioned what I was doing, or tried to slow me down, I would just snap. I'd fly into this intense rage. It wasn't just energy; it was this really volatile mix of feeling unstoppable and then getting incredibly angry if anyone got in my way.
Apart from this recent energetic period, have you ever had times when you felt persistently sad, hopeless, or depressed for several days or longer?

Yeah, I have. Actually, right now, or I guess for a while now, I've been feeling that way. The depressed, shut-down part has been going on for about four months. It's just this heavy, hopeless feeling that doesn't really lift.

When you were hearing Garrett's voice and feeling that intense energy and anger, were you also feeling depressed and hopeless at that same time, or did the depression come after that energetic period ended?

I... I don't think they happened at the exact same time. When I was wired and hearing Garrett, I was just so full of that angry energy. I wasn't feeling sad or hopeless then. The depression... this heavy feeling I have now... that really started after the energy crashed. It didn't overlap, at least not that I can remember. It was more like one ended and the other took over.
During this four-month period of depression that you're experiencing now, have you been hearing Garrett's voice, or has that stopped?

No, it stopped. I only started hearing Garrett's voice during that time when I was all wired up, barely sleeping, and trying to do all those impossible projects. I had never heard him like that before my mood shifted that way. It wasn't something that happened during normal grief, and I haven't heard him since I crashed into this depression.
